data.body_html:
Planning a Marbella family boat day paddleboarding snorkeling trip is one of the best ways to enjoy the Costa del Sol with kids. With calm coves, warm water, and a range of family-friendly boats departing from Puerto Banús, you can create a day that mixes adventure with relaxation. This guide covers the best boats, the top spots for paddleboarding and snorkeling, and what to expect from your charter.

Why choose a boat day for paddleboarding and snorkeling in Marbella?

A private boat gives you access to secluded coves that are hard to reach from shore. You avoid crowded beaches, set your own pace, and have all equipment on board. The Mediterranean water temperature in Marbella reaches 24°C in July and August, making snorkeling comfortable for all ages. Paddleboarding from a boat means you can explore quiet bays like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés without fighting for space.

Best boats for a family day on the water

For small families (up to 5 people), the Dubhe (8m) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m) are nimble and easy to manage. For larger groups, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) and Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) offer more deck space and a cabin. These Tier A boats start at €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for a full 8-hour day – all including skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and VAT. If you want a bigger experience, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) comes with a free jet ski from €4,719 for 4 hours. All depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella.

Top coves for paddleboarding and snorkeling

  • Cala del Faro – A small, sheltered cove west of Marbella with clear, shallow water. Ideal for beginners.
  • Cala Cortés – A rocky cove with good underwater visibility. Snorkelers often see small fish and octopus.
  • Cabopino Beach – A sandy beach near the dunes, with calm conditions and a nearby marina.
  • Río Verde area – Just east of Puerto Banús, this stretch has gentle currents and a sandy bottom.

Your skipper will know the best spots based on wind and tide conditions. All are within a 15–20 minute cruise from Puerto Banús.

What to bring for a family boat day

Pack swimwear, towels, sunscreen (reef-safe if possible), hats, and sunglasses. Bring a change of clothes for after swimming. For kids, consider rash vests for extra sun protection. Paddleboarding and snorkeling gear can be arranged on request – just ask when booking. The boat provides water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light snacks. You can also bring your own food and drinks.

Sample itinerary for a 4-hour family charter

TimeActivity
10:00Board at Puerto Banús, safety briefing, depart
10:30Anchor at Cala del Faro for paddleboarding
11:30Snorkeling session in Cala Cortés
12:30Cruise along the coast, enjoy drinks and snacks
13:00Return to Puerto Banús

For an 8-hour day, add a lunch stop at a beachside chiringuito or a longer swim break at Cabopino.

Safety tips for paddleboarding and snorkeling with kids

Always wear a life jacket when paddleboarding – the skipper will provide them. Snorkel in pairs, and stay close to the boat. The Mediterranean is generally calm, but currents can pick up near headlands. Listen to your skipper’s advice on where and when to go in. Most family-friendly spots have a sandy or rocky bottom with no strong waves.

How to book your family boat day

Contact us via WhatsApp for availability and pricing. We recommend booking at least 24 hours in advance, especially in July and August. Tell us your group size, preferred boat, and any extras like paddleboarding gear. We’ll confirm your charter and send departure details. All charters depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella’s premier marina.

What boats are best for a family day on the water in Marbella?

For small families, the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m, 5 pax) are ideal. For larger groups, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) or Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) offer more space. All depart from Puerto Banús.
